# MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01

Scope
- This maintenance manual covers fastener inspection, torque verification practices, and way lube refill coordination for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01). It applies to maintenance technicians and shift leads performing scheduled or condition-based work on this machine.
- The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours.
- The lubricant part number for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is CFW-LUB-477.
- Use this document together with SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for related safety, lockout/tagout, and lubrication tasks.

Background and rationale
- Fasteners on the machine secure structural components, guards, ways, and motion assemblies. Vibration, thermal cycling from the heat treat process, and cutting forces can lead to loosening or preload loss over time. Regular inspection and controlled torque application reduce the risk of component movement, misalignment, and bearing overload.
- Way lubrication maintains film thickness and prevents metal-to-metal contact. The specified refill interval and lubricant part number are established from vendor guidance and in-plant testing to balance contamination control and service life.
- Torque verification is required after any access that removes or disturbs fasteners on load-bearing or motion-critical components to ensure repeatable preload and to avoid overstress or fatigue.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench appropriate to the fastener head type.
- Socket set and driver handles compatible with the fastener head geometry used on EQ-P1-L4-CN01.
- Fastener-specific bit inserts or washers as required by the fastener design.
- Clean lint-free rags and approved cleaning solvent per SOP-P1-L4-04.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for hard-to-see locations.
- Torque verification witness log sheet and maintenance work order forms.
- Manufacturer fastener details and assembly drawings referenced in the maintenance system; consult SOP-P1-L4-03 for documentation handling.

Procedure
Preparation
- Verify machine is in a safe condition for maintenance per SOP-P1-L4-03 and SOP-P1-L4-05. Ensure lockout/tagout is applied where required and that all energy sources affecting the work area are controlled.
- Gather tools and the correct lubricant CFW-LUB-477. Confirm cleanliness of torque wrench and sockets.

Visual inspection
- Conduct a systematic visual check of all external and accessible internal fasteners associated with guards, covers, baseplates, and motion components. Look for signs of fretting, corrosion, washer deformation, or thread damage. Use mirror or borescope for obscured locations.
- Identify any fasteners showing thread engagement loss or physical damage. Tag compromised fasteners for replacement and generate a work order.

Torque verification and controlled re-torque
- Where fastener preload must be controlled, use the calibrated torque wrench to verify torque. If a fastener is found below expected preload, bring it to the specified assembly procedure requirement for that component, then verify with the torque wrench again.
- For assemblies that require sequential tightening, follow the manufacturer sequence documented in the machine assembly drawings. Use small incremental rotations when seating components to avoid inducing misalignment.
- If a fastener shows signs of yielding, galling, cross-threading, or has damaged head geometry, replace it rather than attempting re-torque.

Way lube refill coordination
- Refill way lube in accordance with the established interval. The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours. Use only lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477 for refills and top-offs to maintain compatibility and additive package consistency.
- Before refill, clean the filler area per SOP-P1-L4-04 to prevent contamination ingress. Record the refill action on the maintenance log and note the lubricant part number used.

Examples and scenarios
- Example: After replacing a spindle housing cover, re-check the perimeter fasteners for torque. If multiple fasteners around the cover show preload loss, suspect seat distortion; loosen and re-seat the cover, clean mating faces, apply specified fasteners or replacements, and re-torque per assembly procedure.
- Example: During routine inspection a technician observes minor oil seepage near a way wiper. Clean the area, replace the wiper if degraded, and perform a way lube top-off using CFW-LUB-477. Log the top-off and plan the next refill based on the operating hours accumulation using the interval provided.

Records to keep
- Maintain a torque verification log with the following entries: equipment id, fastener location description, inspection finding, torque verification outcome, any fastener replacements, technician initials, and work order reference. Archive logs per plant document retention practices and reference SOP-P1-L4-03 for record handling.
- Maintain way lube refill records that include equipment id, lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477, date/time of refill, quantity added, technician initials, and associated work order. Note the operating hour counter at time of refill where available.
- Tag replaced fasteners and retain failed components for analysis when requested. Record part numbers for replacements in the asset history.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners must show no visible thread or head damage and must meet the assembly preload criterion when verified with a calibrated torque wrench. Any fastener that cannot be brought to the required preload without signs of material failure must be replaced.
- Way lubrication must be performed using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477 and logged. The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours and refills must be documented accordingly.
- Maintenance actions are complete when torque verification logs and lubricant refill records are entered into the maintenance management system and a closure note is added to the work order. Refer to SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for related procedural and safety requirements.
